## Dosing information
Usual Adult Dose for Erosive Esophagitis:
Treatment of Erosive Esophagitis: 40 mg orally once a day for up to 8 weeks; however an additional 8 weeks may be considered for patients who have not healed after the initial treatment. Safety and efficacy beyond 16 weeks of therapy have not been established. Maintenance of Healing of Erosive Esophagitis: 40 mg orally once a day. Controlled studies have been limited to 12 months of pantoprazole therapy.
Usual Adult Dose for Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease:
Parenteral: 40 mg once a day for 7 to 10 days, administered via intravenous infusion over a period of 15 minutes. Intravenous therapy should be discontinued as soon as the patient is able to resume oral therapy. Oral: 40 mg orally once a day, for short-term administration (up to 8 weeks); however an additional 8 weeks may be considered for patients who have not healed after the initial treatment. Safety and efficacy beyond 16 weeks of therapy have not been established.
Usual Adult Dose for Duodenal Ulcer:
Study (n=54) 40 mg orally once a day, dose was increased every 12 weeks by 40 mg increments to a maximum of 120 mg per day, for 28 weeks. Data have revealed that monotherapy with daily doses of 40 mg have been associated with complete duodenal ulcer healing in up to 87% and 94% of patients after 4 weeks and 8 weeks respectively.
Usual Adult Dose for Gastric Ulcer:
40 mg orally once a day. Data have revealed that monotherapy with daily doses of 40 mg have been associated with complete gastric ulcer healing in up to 87% and 97% of patients after 4 weeks and 8 weeks respectively.
Usual Adult Dose for Helicobacter pylori Infection:
Study (n=242) - Triple therapy: 40 mg orally twice daily for 7 days, commonly in conjunction with clarithromycin and either amoxicillin or metronidazole to eradicate Helicobacter pylori, followed with 40 mg pantoprazole orally once daily until day 28. Triple therapy has resulted in eradication rates of greater than 95%. The QUADRATE Study (n=405) - Quadruple therapy: 40 mg orally twice daily for 7 days, concomitantly with bismuth subcitrate and tetracycline, both four times daily, and metronidazole 200 mg three times daily and 400 mg at bedtime. Helicobacter Pylori eradication was achieved in 82% of patients.
Usual Adult Dose for Zollinger-Ellison Syndrome:
Parenteral: 80 mg every 12 hours, administered by 15-minute infusion. Daily doses higher than 240 mg administered in equally divided doses by 15-minute infusion, or administered for more than 6 days have not been studied. Oral: 40 mg twice daily, to a maximum of 240 mg per day. Some patients have received treatment with pantoprazole for more than 2 years.
Usual Adult Dose for Stress Ulcer Prophylaxis:
Study (n=21) - Stress Ulcer bleeding prophylaxis in the Critical Care Setting: 80 mg twice daily, as a bolus infusion over a period of 15 minutes, to a maximum daily dose of 240 mg, divided into three equal doses. Study (n=20) - Peptic Ulcer rebleeding prophylaxis after hemostasis in the Critical Care Setting: 80 mg IV bolus, followed by continuous infusion of 8 mg/hr for 3 days, after which therapy may be continued with an oral PPI.
Usual Adult Dose for Peptic Ulcer:
Study (n=21) - Stress Ulcer bleeding prophylaxis in the Critical Care Setting: 80 mg twice daily, as a bolus infusion over a period of 15 minutes, to a maximum daily dose of 240 mg, divided into three equal doses. Study (n=20) - Peptic Ulcer rebleeding prophylaxis after hemostasis in the Critical Care Setting: 80 mg IV bolus, followed by continuous infusion of 8 mg/hr for 3 days, after which therapy may be continued with an oral PPI.

## How should I use albuterol inhalation?
Use albuterol inhalation exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Follow all directions on your prescription label. Do not use albuterol inhalation in larger or smaller amounts or for longer than recommended.
Read all patient information, medication guides, and instruction sheets provided to you. Ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions.
You may need to prime your albuterol inhaler device before the first use. Your medicine comes with directions for priming if needed. You may also need to shake your albuterol device just before each use.
Keeping your inhaler clean is important to ensure you are receiving the medication. Clean the plastic actuator with the canister removed at least once a week. Your medicine comes with directions for properly cleaning your device.
Follow all medication instructions very carefully.
Do not allow a young child to use albuterol inhalation without help from an adult.
The usual dose of albuterol inhalation is 2 inhalations every 4 to 6 hours. To prevent exercise-induced bronchospasm, use 2 inhalations 15 to 30 minutes before you exercise. The effects of albuterol inhalation should last about 4 to 6 hours.
Seek medical attention if you think your asthma medications are not working as well. An increased need for medication could be an early sign of a serious asthma attack.
Use the dose counter on your albuterol inhaler device and get your prescription refilled before you run out of medicine completely. Always use the new inhaler device provided with your refill. Do not float a medicine canister in water to see if it is empty.
ProAir HFA, Proventil HFA, or Ventolin HFA must be shaken before each use. You do not need to shake ProAir RespiClick before using.
Follow all product instructions on how to clean your albuterol inhaler device and mouthpiece. Do not wash or put any part of the ProAir RespiClick inhaler device in water. Do not use a spacer or volume holding chamber with ProAir RespiClick.
Asthma is often treated with a combination of drugs. Use all medications as directed by your doctor. Read the medication guide or patient instructions provided with each medication. Do not change your doses or medication schedule without your doctor's advice.
Store at room temperature away from moisture, heat, or cold temperatures.
Keep the albuterol canister away from open flame or high heat, such as in a car on a hot day. The canister may explode if it gets too hot. Do not puncture or burn an empty inhaler canister.

## How should I take potassium chloride?
Take potassium chloride exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Follow all directions on your prescription label and read all medication guides or instruction sheets. Your doctor may occasionally change your dose.
Read and carefully follow any Instructions for Use provided with your medicine. Ask your doctor or pharmacist if you do not understand these instructions.
Take potassium chloride with a full glass of water. Take potassium chloride with food or just after a meal.
Measure liquid medicine with the dosing syringe provided, or with a special dose-measuring spoon or medicine cup. If you do not have a dose-measuring device, ask your pharmacist for one.
Do not crush, chew, or suck on a tablet or capsule. Sucking on the pill could irritate your mouth or throat.
Call your doctor if you have trouble swallowing a potassium chloride capsule or tablet. You may be able to dissolve the tablet in water, or mix the medicine from a capsule with soft food. Carefully follow your doctor's instructions.
Mix the powder form of this medicine with at least 4 ounces (one-half cup) of cold water or fruit juice before taking. Drink the mixture slowly, over 5 to 10 minutes in all. To make sure you get the entire dose, add a little more water to the same glass, swirl gently and drink right away.
To be sure this medicine is helping your condition, you may need frequent blood tests. You may not notice any change in your symptoms, but your blood work will help your doctor determine how long to treat you with potassium chloride. Even if you have no symptoms, tests can help your doctor determine if this medicine is effective.
Your treatment may include a special diet. Follow the diet plan created for you by your doctor or nutrition counselor. Get familiar with the list of foods you should eat or avoid to help control your condition.

Some tablets are made with a shell that is not absorbed or melted in the body. Part of this shell may appear in your stool. This is normal and will not make the medicine less effective.

## Cyclobenzaprine dosage
The usual cyclobenzaprine dose for muscle spasm is 5 mg three times a day, which may be increased to 10 mg three times a day if needed. The maximum dose is 30 mg per day. Cyclobenzaprine is taken for a maximum of 2 to 3 weeks. 1
Cyclobenzaprine dosage chart:
Immediate-release tablets: the usual starting dose is 5 mg three times a day, increased to 10 mg three times a day based on your response. In adults 65 and older and in people with mild liver problems, treatment should start at 5 mg and be increased slowly, if at all. The tablets are not recommended with moderate to severe liver impairment. 1
Amrix extended-release capsules: the recommended dose is 15 mg once daily for most adults; some people may need 30 mg once daily (one 30 mg capsule or two 15 mg capsules). Amrix is not recommended in adults 65 and older, or in anyone with liver impairment of any severity. 2
Tonmya sublingual tablets (fibromyalgia): The recommended starting dose of Tonmya is 2.8 mg (1 sublingual tablet) once daily at bedtime for the first 14 days, then increases to the target dose of 5.6 mg (2 sublingual tablets) once daily at bedtime from day 15 onward. The maximum is 5.6 mg once daily. In adults 65 and older and in people with mild liver impairment, the maximum is 2.8 mg once daily at bedtime, and Tonmya is not recommended with moderate or severe liver impairment. 3
Product | Usual adult dose | Maximum dose | How long
Immediate-release tablets, formerly sold as Flexeril (adults and children 15 and older) | 5 mg three times a day, increased to 10 mg three times a day if needed | 30 mg per day (10 mg three times a day) | Up to 2 to 3 weeks
Amrix extended-release capsules | 15 mg once daily | 30 mg once daily | Up to 2 to 3 weeks
Tonmya sublingual tablets (fibromyalgia) | 2.8 mg once daily at bedtime for 14 days, then 5.6 mg once daily at bedtime | 5.6 mg once daily | Ongoing, as directed
1,2,3
Can I take 2 cyclobenzaprine 10 mg at the same time?:
No. Do not take two cyclobenzaprine 10 mg tablets at once. The maximum recommended single dose of the immediate-release tablet is 10 mg, taken up to three times a day. Taking 20 mg at one time increases the risk of side effects such as severe drowsiness and fast heart rate, and in overdose cyclobenzaprine can cause dangerous heart rhythm problems, without providing better muscle spasm relief. If your dose is not controlling your symptoms, talk with your doctor rather than doubling up. 1
How often can you take cyclobenzaprine?:
Immediate-release tablets are taken three times a day. Amrix extended-release capsules and Tonmya sublingual tablets are taken once a day. Do not take extra doses between scheduled doses. 1,2,3
How long does cyclobenzaprine take to work, and how long does it last?:
In clinical trials of the immediate-release tablets, the muscle relaxant effect was measurable within the first several days, with significant improvement in muscle spasm and pain by day 3 or 4 of treatment. 1
With Amrix extended-release capsules, the drug is first detectable in the blood about 1.5 hours after a dose, with peak levels at 7 to 8 hours, and one daily dose provides day-long coverage. 2
How long does cyclobenzaprine stay in your system?:
Cyclobenzaprine stays in your system for about 3 to 7 days after your last dose. It has a half-life of around 18 hours for the immediate-release tablets, and a drug takes 4 to 5 half-lives to clear from the body. 1
The once-daily forms last longer: the half-life is about 32 hours for Amrix extended-release capsules and about 36 hours for Tonmya sublingual tablets, so these can take a week or more to fully clear. Cyclobenzaprine also stays in the body longer in older adults and in people with liver problems, in whom blood levels run higher. 1,2,3
Does cyclobenzaprine show up on a drug test?:
No, cyclobenzaprine does not usually show up on a drug test, as it is not a controlled substance and it is not one of the five substances (amphetamines, cannabinoids, cocaine, opiates, and phencyclidine) required on standard federal workplace drug tests. 3,5
However, cyclobenzaprine has a similar structure to tricyclic antidepressants, and it is a recognized cause of false positive results on tricyclic antidepressant immunoassays, including urine immunoassays. Tests for tricyclic antidepressants are not part of routine drugs-of-abuse screening. 5
If you take cyclobenzaprine and need a drug test, tell the testing provider what medicines you take. A screening result is only presumptive, and a confirmatory laboratory test such as gas chromatography-mass spectrometry can tell cyclobenzaprine apart from a tricyclic antidepressant. 5

Common side effects:
The most common side effects may include headache, nausea, muscle aches and pains, weakness, and constipation.
Serious side effects:
Rosuvastatin may cause serious side effects, including:

## Warnings
Meloxicam can increase your risk of a fatal heart attack or stroke, especially if you use it long term or take high doses, or if you have heart disease. Even people without heart disease or risk factors could have a stroke or heart attack while taking this medicine.
Do not use this medicine just before or after heart bypass surgery (coronary artery bypass graft, or CABG).
Avoid taking meloxicam after a recent heart attack, unless your doctor tells you to. You may have an increased risk of another heart attack if you take this medicine after a recent heart attack.
Get emergency medical help if you have chest pain, weakness, shortness of breath, slurred speech, or problems with vision or balance.
Meloxicam may also cause stomach or intestinal bleeding, which can be fatal. These conditions can occur without warning while you are using this medicine, especially in older adults.
Call your doctor at once if you have symptoms of stomach bleeding, such as black, bloody, or tarry stools, or coughing up blood or vomit that looks like coffee grounds.
Avoid smoking and drinking alcohol, as they also increase your risk of stomach bleeding.

## How should I take prednisone?
Take prednisone exactly as prescribed, with food or milk to protect your stomach. Your doctor will often start you on a higher dose and then lower it. Do not change your dose or stop the medicine without advice.
- Take your dose in the morning if your doctor tells you to. Your adrenal glands are most active between 2 am and 8 am, and taking a steroid at that time interferes with them the least. A morning dose may also help you sleep better, though that is a separate benefit.
- Swallow delayed-release tablets whole. Do not crush, break, or chew them.
- Measure liquid prednisone with a marked oral syringe, dosing spoon or medicine cup, not a kitchen spoon. Use the dropper that comes with the concentrated solution.
- You may mix the concentrated solution with juice or a soft food such as applesauce.
- Tell your doctor if you have a serious illness, a fever, an infection, surgery, or a medical emergency. You may need a higher dose for a short time.
- You may need regular blood tests, blood pressure checks and eye checks during long-term treatment.
- Wear a medical alert tag or carry a card saying you take a steroid.
- Store prednisone at room temperature, away from moisture and heat. Throw away any unused concentrated solution 90 days after you first open the bottle.

Semaglutide FDA-approved uses for each brand are Ozempic (type 2 diabetes, reducing cardiovascular event risks, reducing risk of kidney function decline), Wegovy (weight management, reducing cardiovascular event risks, non-cirrhotic MASH), and Rybelsus (type 2 diabetes, reducing cardiovascular event risks).

## Before taking this medicine
Tell your doctor about all your medical conditions and medications before starting fluoxetine (Prozac), as some may interact with it or affect whether it is safe for you.
Tell your doctor if you take any of the following medications or supplements:
- Triptans (for migraine)
- Antidepressants or mood stabilizers, including SSRIs, SNRIs, tricyclics, MAOIs, lithium, buspirone, or antipsychotics
- Amphetamines
- Opioid pain medications, including tramadol, fentanyl, meperidine, or methadone
- Over-the-counter supplements such as St. John's Wort or tryptophan
- Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT)
Many of these combinations can increase the risk of serotonin syndrome, a potentially serious condition.
Tell your doctor if you have or have had any of the following:
- Liver, kidney, or heart problems
- Seizures or epilepsy
- Bipolar disorder or mania
- Low sodium levels in the blood
- A stroke or high blood pressure
- Bleeding problems
Pregnancy
Tell your healthcare provider if you are pregnant, become pregnant, or plan to become pregnant while taking fluoxetine tablets. Using fluoxetine later in pregnancy may increase the risk of complications in the newborn, including problems that need a longer hospital stay, breathing support, or tube feeding, and a serious lung condition called persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn (PPHN). Untreated depression also carries risks in pregnancy, so discuss the benefits and risks of treatment with your healthcare provider rather than stopping on your own.
If you become pregnant while taking fluoxetine tablets, ask your healthcare provider about joining the National Pregnancy Registry for Antidepressants, which tracks pregnancy outcomes in women who take these medicines. You can enroll by calling 1-866-961-2388 or visiting womensmentalhealth.org.
Breastfeeding:
Fluoxetine passes into breast milk. Tell your healthcare provider if you are breastfeeding or plan to breastfeed, and discuss the best way to feed your baby while you are taking fluoxetine tablets. If you do breastfeed, watch your baby for agitation, irritability, poor feeding, or poor weight gain, and seek medical advice if you notice any of these.

## What is losartan?
Losartan is used alone or in combination with other medications to treat high blood pressure in adults and children at least 6 years old.
Losartan is also used to decrease the risk of stroke in people who have high blood pressure and a heart condition called left ventricular hypertrophy (enlargement of the walls of the left side of the heart).

## What is the usual spironolactone dosage?
The usual starting dose of spironolactone tablets for adults is 25 mg to 100 mg a day, depending on the condition being treated. Your doctor will pick a starting dose and then adjust it based on your blood tests and how you respond.
Spironolactone dosage for heart failure:
Treatment starts at spironolactone 25 mg once a day, provided your potassium level is 5.0 mEq/L or lower and your kidney function (eGFR) is above 50. If you tolerate that, the dose may go up to 50 mg once a day. If your potassium rises too high, the dose may drop to 25 mg every other day. If your eGFR is between 30 and 50, your doctor may start you at 25 mg every other day because of the higher risk of high potassium.
Spironolactone dosage for high blood pressure:
The usual starting dose is spironolactone 25 mg to 100 mg a day, taken as one dose or split into two. The dose can be adjusted every two weeks. Doses above 100 mg a day do not generally lower blood pressure any further.
Spironolactone dosage for fluid build-up (edema):
The usual starting dose is 100 mg a day, taken as one dose or split into two, and the dose can range from 25 mg to 200 mg a day. If you have cirrhosis, treatment is started in hospital and increased slowly. When spironolactone is the only water pill being used, it is given for at least five days before the dose is increased.
Spironolactone dosage for primary hyperaldosteronism:
The dose is 100 mg to 400 mg a day when preparing for surger y. For people who are not suitable for surgery, the lowest dose that works is used long term.
Spironolactone oral liquid doses:
The oral liquid has its own separate doses because it is absorbed differently. Heart failure starts at 20 mg (4 mL) once a day. High blood pressure starts at 20 mg (4 mL) to 75 mg (15 mL) a day. Swelling from cirrhosis starts at 75 mg (15 mL) a day, begun in hospital. If more than 100 mg a day is needed, a different form of the medicine should be used instead.
Spironolactone formulations:
- Spironolactone 25 mg tablets
- Spironolactone 50 mg tablets
- Spironolactone 100 mg tablets
- Spironolactone oral suspension 25 mg per 5 mL

## How should I use tirzepatide?
You should follow the directions on your prescription label carefully and ask your pharmacist or doctor to explain any part you do not understand. It is important to use this medicine exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it or take it more often than prescribed by your doctor.
Tirzepatide is injected under the skin (subcutaneously) using a pre-filled single-dose pen, a multi-dose KwikPen (for single patient use), and a single-dose vial with a syringe. Do not stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor.
Tirzepatide KwikPen:
The KwikPen contains 4 fixed doses, and one dose is injected weekly (subcutaneously).
- For your weekly dose, you need to turn the dose knob all the way until it stops AND the 1 icon is in the dose window.

- Do not share your tirzepatide Pen with other people, even if the pen needle has been changed. You may give other people a serious infection or get a serious infection from them.

## Hydrochlorothiazide FAQ
Does hydrochlorothiazide cause weight loss?:
Hydrochlorothiazide is not a weight loss medicine. Some people see the number on the scales drop in the first days or weeks of treatment, but this is extra fluid leaving the body rather than any loss of body fat, and it levels off. Do not take hydrochlorothiazide to lose weight.
Can you drink alcohol while taking hydrochlorothiazide?:
Alcohol can make the drop in blood pressure that happens when you stand up worse, which may leave you feeling dizzy or faint. The same applies to barbiturates and opioid pain medicines. Tell your doctor how much you drink so they can advise you.
Does hydrochlorothiazide lower your potassium?:
Yes. Hydrochlorothiazide can lower blood potassium (hypokalemia), and this is more likely at higher doses, when fluid is lost quickly, if you have severe cirrhosis, or after taking the medicine for a long time. Your doctor will check your potassium with blood tests. Tell them if you have muscle cramps, unusual weakness or tiredness, or an irregular heartbeat.
Should you eat more potassium while taking hydrochlorothiazide?:
Only if your doctor tells you to. Low potassium can sometimes be managed with potassium-rich foods, a potassium supplement, or a different type of diuretic that holds on to potassium. Do not start any of these yourself, because too much potassium can also be harmful, and some people on hydrochlorothiazide do not need extra potassium at all.
Is hydrochlorothiazide 12.5mg enough?:
For many people it is. In published trials comparing the two doses, 12.5 mg kept most of the blood pressure reduction seen with 25 mg, and low potassium was consistently less common at 12.5 mg. Starting at 12.5 mg is recommended for adults over 65. Your doctor will decide the right dose for you and may adjust it over time.

## Warnings
Levothyroxine should not be used to treat obesity or weight problems. Dangerous side effects or death can occur from the misuse of this medicine, especially if you are taking any other weight-loss medications or appetite suppressants.
Taking more than your recommended dose will not make this medicine more effective, and may cause serious side effects.
Levothyroxine has a narrow therapeutic index, which means the difference between too little and too much is small. Taking too much or too little over time can affect your heart, bones, blood sugar, cholesterol, digestion, memory and concentration, fertility, and, in children, growth and development. Your doctor will start you on a suitable dose and adjust it gradually based on blood tests.
You may not be able to use levothyroxine if you have certain medical conditions. Tell your doctor if you have an untreated or uncontrolled adrenal gland disorder or any heart problems such as a recent heart attack.
If you have an adrenal gland problem, you will need to start treatment with a steroid (glucocorticoid) medicine before you start levothyroxine. Starting levothyroxine first can trigger a sudden, serious drop in adrenal hormones known as an adrenal crisis.
Older adults and people with heart disease are usually started on a lower dose, because too much thyroid hormone can cause an irregular heartbeat (most commonly atrial fibrillation), angina, or other heart problems. Tell your doctor if you develop chest pain, breathlessness, or a fast or irregular heartbeat.
Taking more levothyroxine than your body needs over a long period can weaken your bones and lead to a higher risk of fractures. This is more likely after menopause. Your doctor will aim to give you the lowest dose that controls your thyroid levels.
Oral levothyroxine should not be used to treat myxedema coma. Levothyroxine given into a vein is used instead.

## Metoprolol dosage
The usual starting dose is 25 mg to 100 mg once a day for extended-release metoprolol, and 100 mg a day for immediate-release metoprolol. Your dose is then adjusted at intervals of a week or longer until your blood pressure or symptoms are controlled.
Metoprolol tartrate (immediate-release tablets) dosage for adults:
Condition | Starting dose | Usual range
High blood pressure | 100 mg a day, as one dose or split into two | 100 mg to 450 mg a day. Doses above 450 mg a day have not been studied.
Angina | 100 mg a day, split into two doses | 100 mg to 400 mg a day. Doses above 400 mg a day have not been studied.
After a heart attack | 50 mg every 6 hours for 48 hours, starting 15 minutes after the last dose given into a vein. If the full intravenous dose was not tolerated, 25 mg is used. | Maintenance is 100 mg twice a day, continued for at least 3 months.
With immediate-release tablets, a once-daily dose may not keep blood pressure controlled for the full 24 hours, especially at 100 mg. Splitting the dose or taking a larger daily dose may be needed.
Metoprolol succinate (extended-release tablets and capsules) dosage for adults:
Condition | Starting dose | Usual range
High blood pressure | 25 mg to 100 mg once a day | Adjust weekly or less often. Doses above 400 mg a day have not been studied.
Angina | 100 mg once a day | Increase weekly until symptoms are controlled or your heart rate slows noticeably. Doses above 400 mg a day have not been studied.
Heart failure | 25 mg once a day for two weeks, or 12.5 mg once a day in more severe heart failure | Double the dose every two weeks to the highest dose you tolerate, up to 200 mg once a day.
Kapspargo Sprinkle capsules are not suitable to start heart failure treatment if a dose below 25 mg is needed.
Metoprolol dosage for children:
Extended-release metoprolol is the only form approved for children, and only for high blood pressure in children aged 6 years and older. The starting dose is 1 mg for each kilogram of body weight once a day, up to a maximum first dose of 50 mg. Doses above 2 mg/kg, or above 200 mg a day, have not been studied. Extended-release metoprolol has not been studied in children under 6 years.
Dose adjustments:
- Liver problems. Start at a lower dose than usual and increase slowly.
- Kidney problems. No dose reduction is needed.
- Older adults. A low starting dose is generally used, because liver, kidney, and heart function are more often reduced and other medicines are more often involved.
- Switching between forms. When changing from immediate-release to extended-release metoprolol, the same total daily dose is used.

## Sertraline side effects
Common sertraline side effects:
The most common sertraline side effects are nausea, diarrhea or loose stools, trouble sleeping, dry mouth, tiredness, dizziness, sleepiness, tremor, indigestion, agitation, reduced appetite, increased sweating, and sexual problems.
The table below shows how often each side effect was reported in pooled placebo-controlled trials in 3,066 adults, compared with 2,293 people taking placebo.
Side effect | Sertraline | Placebo
Nausea | 26% | 12%
Diarrhea or loose stools | 20% | 10%
Insomnia (trouble sleeping) | 20% | 13%
Dry mouth | 14% | 9%
Fatigue (tiredness) | 12% | 8%
Dizziness | 12% | 8%
Somnolence (sleepiness) | 11% | 6%
Tremor (shaking) | 9% | 2%
Dyspepsia (indigestion) | 8% | 4%
Agitation | 8% | 5%
Decreased appetite | 7% | 2%
Hyperhidrosis (heavy sweating) | 7% | 3%
Constipation | 6% | 4%
Decreased libido (lower sex drive) | 6% | 2%
Palpitations | 4% | 2%
Visual impairment | 4% | 2%
Vomiting | 4% | 1%
Some side effects were more common with particular conditions. Sleepiness was more common in depression trials, insomnia and agitation in OCD trials, constipation and agitation in panic disorder trials, tiredness in PTSD trials, and insomnia, dizziness, tiredness, dry mouth, and a general feeling of being unwell in social anxiety disorder trials. In PMDD trials, sleepiness, dry mouth, dizziness, tiredness, and stomach pain were more common.
In these trials, 12% of people taking sertraline stopped treatment because of a side effect, compared with 4% of people taking placebo. The most common reasons for stopping were nausea (3%), diarrhea (2%), agitation (2%), and insomnia (2%).
Sexual side effects of sertraline:
SSRIs including sertraline can cause sexual problems. In men, this can mean delayed ejaculation or being unable to ejaculate, lower sex drive, and difficulty getting or keeping an erection. In women, it can mean lower sex drive and delayed orgasm or being unable to have an orgasm.
Sexual side effect | Sertraline | Placebo
Ejaculation failure (men) | 8% | 1%
Decreased libido (men) | 7% | 2%
Erectile dysfunction (men) | 4% | 1%
Ejaculation disorder (men) | 3% | 0%
Male sexual dysfunction | 2% | 0%
Decreased libido (women) | 4% | 2%
Changes in sex drive and sexual function can also be part of depression and anxiety themselves, so the timing of when symptoms started matters. These numbers may underestimate how often sexual side effects happen, because people and their providers do not always raise the subject. Tell your provider about any change in sexual function, since there may be ways to manage it.
Serious sertraline side effects:
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to sertraline: rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty breathing.
Call your doctor at once if you have:
- signs of serotonin syndrome, which can be life threatening: agitation, hallucinations, confusion, coma or other changes in mental state, a racing heartbeat, high or low blood pressure, dizziness, heavy sweating, fever, muscle stiffness, twitching or overactive reflexes, loss of coordination, seizures, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea;
- unusual bleeding or bruising, including nosebleeds, bleeding gums, blood in vomit or stools, or black tarry stools;
- signs of a manic episode: greatly increased energy, severe trouble sleeping, racing thoughts, reckless behavior, unusually grand ideas, excessive happiness or irritability, or talking more or faster than usual;
- seizures or convulsions;
- eye pain, changes in vision, or swelling or redness in or around the eye, which can be signs of angle-closure glaucoma (a sudden rise in pressure inside the eye);
- signs of low sodium in the blood (hyponatremia): headache, trouble concentrating or thinking, memory problems, confusion, weakness, or feeling unsteady, which can lead to falls. Severe cases have caused hallucinations, fainting, seizures, coma, and death;
- fainting, chest discomfort, or an irregular heartbeat, which can be signs of a heart rhythm problem called QTc prolongation.
Sertraline side effects in children and teenagers:
The overall pattern of side effects in 281 children and teenagers treated with sertraline was generally similar to that seen in adults. Side effects reported in at least 2% of children and teenagers, and at least twice as often as with placebo, that were not common in adults were fever, hyperkinesia (abnormally increased movement), urinary incontinence, aggression, nosebleeds, purpura (purple spots under the skin), joint pain, weight loss, muscle twitching, and anxiety.
Reduced appetite and weight loss have been seen with SSRIs, so height and weight should be monitored during treatment.

Less common side effects reported during studies include tachycardia (fast heartbeat), tinnitus (ringing in the ears), underactive thyroid, enlarged pupils, blurred vision, blood in the stools, swelling, unsteady walking, irritability, fever, raised liver enzymes, anaphylaxis, diabetes, high cholesterol, low blood sugar, increased appetite, joint pain, muscle spasms, poor coordination, coma, convulsions, reduced alertness, numbness, lethargy, restlessness, fainting, aggression, teeth grinding, confusion, euphoric mood, hallucination, blood in the urine, milk production from the breasts, priapism (a long-lasting erection), vaginal bleeding, wheezing, yawning, hair loss, cold sweats, skin inflammation, blistering, itching, rash, hives, bleeding, high blood pressure, and flushing.
Side effects reported after sertraline came onto the market include increased clotting times, AV block, slow heartbeat, atrial arrhythmias, QTc prolongation, ventricular tachycardia including Torsade de Pointes, breast enlargement in men, raised prolactin, irregular periods, SIADH, blindness, optic neuritis, cataract, severe liver problems including hepatitis, jaundice, and liver failure with some fatal outcomes, pancreatitis, several blood disorders, angioedema, low sodium, high blood sugar, rhabdomyolysis (muscle breakdown), lockjaw, serotonin syndrome, movement disorders including akathisia and dystonia, psychosis, bedwetting, nightmares, sudden kidney failure, pulmonary hypertension, eosinophilic pneumonia, loss of smell, photosensitivity, severe skin reactions such as Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, spasm of blood vessels in the brain, and vasculitis.
This is not a complete list of side effects, and others may occur. Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects. You may report side effects to the FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.

## Dosing information
Usual adult dose for edema associated with congestive heart failure, cirrhosis of the liver, and chronic renal disease (including nephrotic syndrome):
Oral: initial dose 20 to 80 mg orally once. This may be repeated at the same dose or increased by 20 or 40 mg no sooner than 6 to 8 hours after the previous dose, until the desired diuretic effect has been obtained.
Maintenance dose: administer the dose that provided the desired diuretic effect once or twice a day (for example, at 8 am and 2 pm).
Comments: edema may be most efficiently and safely mobilized by giving this drug on 2 to 4 consecutive days each week. When doses greater than 80 mg/day are given for prolonged periods, careful clinical observation and laboratory monitoring are particularly advisable.
Usual Furoscix adult and pediatric 43 kg and above dose (ReadyFlow autoinjector):
- 80 mg of furosemide given subcutaneously in about 10 seconds.
Usual Furoscix adult and pediatric 43 kg and above dose (On-Body Infusor):
- 30 mg of furosemide over the first hour, then 12.5 mg per hour for the subsequent 4 hours. This dose is delivered automatically by the On-Body Infusor.
- In children weighing at least 43 kg, the device must be applied by a healthcare provider or adult caregiver.
Furoscix is not for chronic use and should be replaced with oral diuretics as soon as practical. People with significantly reduced kidney function may need additional diuretic therapy, because both Furoscix devices deliver a fixed 80 mg dose.
Usual adult furosemide dose for pulmonary edema:
IV: 40 mg IV slowly over 1 to 2 minutes. If a satisfactory response does not occur within one hour, this may be increased to 80 mg IV slowly over 1 to 2 minutes.

## Boxed warning: suicidal thoughts and behaviors
Sertraline carries a boxed warning, the FDA's most serious type of warning. Antidepressants increased the risk of suicidal thoughts and behavior in children, teenagers, and young adults in short-term studies.
In pooled analyses of placebo-controlled antidepressant trials covering about 77,000 adults and more than 4,500 children and teenagers, the risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviors in people aged 24 and under was higher with an antidepressant than with placebo. The risk varied considerably between different antidepressants, and it also varied by condition, with the highest rate in people being treated for depression. The difference between antidepressant and placebo, per 1,000 patients treated, was:
Age (years) | Difference compared with placebo
Under 18 | 14 more patients with suicidal thoughts or behaviors
18 to 24 | 5 more patients
25 to 64 | 1 fewer patient
65 and over | 6 fewer patients
It is not known whether this risk continues beyond about four months of treatment. There is good evidence that antidepressants delay depression coming back in adults, and depression itself raises the risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviors.
Anyone taking sertraline should be watched closely for worsening symptoms and for new or sudden changes in mood, behavior, thoughts, or feelings, especially in the first few months of treatment and whenever the dose is changed. Call your healthcare provider right away, or call 911 in an emergency, if you notice:
- thoughts about suicide or dying, or attempts to harm yourself
- new or worse depression, anxiety, or panic attacks
- feeling agitated, restless, angry, or irritable
- acting aggressive or violent, or acting on dangerous impulses
- trouble sleeping
- a big increase in activity or talking more than is normal for you
- any other unusual change in behavior or mood
Tell family members or caregivers which symptoms to watch for, so they can call your provider if you are not able to.

## Semaglutide side effects
Common semaglutide side effects:
Common semaglutide side effects may include upset stomach, heartburn, burping, gas, bloating, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, loss of appetite, diarrhea, constipation, stomach flu symptoms, low blood sugar (in people with type 2 diabetes), headache, dizziness, tiredness, hair loss, and changes in skin sensations.
Stomach or gastrointestinal side effects are common, but they tend to be mild and clear up in a few weeks and usually will not interfere with long-term treatment. Stomach side effects can be more common with higher doses.
Tips for managing stomach side effects:
Following these tips may help you manage stomach semaglutide side effects:
- Eat more slowly
- Eat smaller meals
- Choose more bland, low-fat foods (like crackers, toast, and rice)
- Avoid eating greasy, fried foods or sugar treats
- Eat foods that contain water (like soup or gelatin)
- Do not lie down right after eating
- Drink clear or ice-cold liquids
- If possible, go outside for fresh air if you feel sick to your stomach
- Ryebelsus is not recommended in patients with severe gastroparesis.
Tips for managing low blood sugar levels (hypoglycemia) side effects:
- Test blood sugar levels regularly if you are also taking diabetic medicines, including insulin or sulphonylureas (e.g., glibenclamide/glyburide, glipizide, and gliclazide) and when you increase your semaglutide dose.
- Your prescriber might reduce your dose of insulin or sulphonylureas if needed to reduce the risk of hypoglycemia
- Symptoms of low blood sugar levels include:
- Treatment for hypoglycemia
- Severe hypoglycemia may require a glucagon injection.
Serious semaglutide side effects:
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction: hives, itching, dizziness, fast heartbeats, difficulty breathing, swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat.
Call your doctor at once if you have:
- vision changes;
- unusual mood changes, thoughts about hurting yourself;
- pounding heartbeats or fluttering in your chest;
- a light-headed feeling, like you might pass out;
- signs of a thyroid tumor - swelling or a lump in your neck, trouble swallowing, a hoarse voice, feeling short of breath;
- symptoms of pancreatitis - severe pain in your upper stomach spreading to your back, nausea with or without vomiting, fast heart rate;
- gallbladder problems - upper stomach pain, fever, clay-colored stools, jaundice (yellowing of the skin or eyes);
- low blood sugar - headache, hunger, weakness, sweating, confusion, irritability, dizziness, fast heart rate, or feeling jittery;
- kidney problems - swelling, urinating less, feeling tired or short of breath; or
- stomach flu symptoms - stomach cramps, vomiting, loss of appetite, diarrhea (may be watery or bloody); or severe stomach problems like severe constipation, fecal impaction, or intestinal obstruction.
This is not a complete list of side effects, and others may occur. Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects. You may report side effects to the FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.

## How should I take metformin?
Take metformin exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Follow all directions on your prescription label and read all medication guides or instruction sheets. Your doctor may occasionally change your dose. Use the medicine exactly as directed.
Take metformin with a meal, unless your doctor tells you otherwise. Some forms of metformin are taken only once daily with the evening meal. Follow your doctor's instructions.
Take immediate release tablets in divided doses 2 to 3 times a day with meals. Your dose will be increased slowly to minimise gastrointestinal side effects.
Do not crush, chew, or break an extended-release tablet. Swallow it whole.
Measure liquid medicine carefully. Shake the oral suspension before you measure a dose. Use the dosing syringe provided, or use a medicine dose-measuring device (not a kitchen spoon).
Some tablets are made with a shell that is not absorbed or melted in the body. Part of this shell may appear in your stool. This is normal and will not make the medicine less effective.
You may have low blood sugar (hypoglycemia) and feel very hungry, dizzy, irritable, confused, anxious, or shaky. To quickly treat hypoglycemia, eat or drink a fast-acting source of sugar (fruit juice, hard candy, crackers, raisins, or non-diet soda).
Your doctor may prescribe a glucagon injection kit in case you have severe hypoglycemia. Be sure your family or close friends know how to give you this injection in an emergency.
Blood sugar levels can be affected by stress, illness, surgery, exercise, alcohol use, or skipping meals. Ask your doctor before changing your dose or medication schedule.
Metformin is only part of a complete treatment program that may also include diet, exercise, weight control, regular blood sugar testing, and special medical care. Follow your doctor's instructions very closely.
Store at room temperature away from moisture, heat, and light.
Your doctor may have you take extra vitamin B12 while you are taking this medicine. Take only the amount of vitamin B12 that your doctor has prescribed.

## Metoprolol dosage
The usual starting dose is 25 mg to 100 mg once a day for extended-release metoprolol, and 100 mg a day for immediate-release metoprolol. Your dose is then adjusted at intervals of a week or longer until your blood pressure or symptoms are controlled.
Metoprolol tartrate (immediate-release tablets) dosage for adults:
Condition | Starting dose | Usual range
High blood pressure | 100 mg a day, as one dose or split into two | 100 mg to 450 mg a day. Doses above 450 mg a day have not been studied.
Angina | 100 mg a day, split into two doses | 100 mg to 400 mg a day. Doses above 400 mg a day have not been studied.
After a heart attack | 50 mg every 6 hours for 48 hours, starting 15 minutes after the last dose given into a vein. If the full intravenous dose was not tolerated, 25 mg is used. | Maintenance is 100 mg twice a day, continued for at least 3 months.
With immediate-release tablets, a once-daily dose may not keep blood pressure controlled for the full 24 hours, especially at 100 mg. Splitting the dose or taking a larger daily dose may be needed.
Metoprolol succinate (extended-release tablets and capsules) dosage for adults:
Condition | Starting dose | Usual range
High blood pressure | 25 mg to 100 mg once a day | Adjust weekly or less often. Doses above 400 mg a day have not been studied.
Angina | 100 mg once a day | Increase weekly until symptoms are controlled or your heart rate slows noticeably. Doses above 400 mg a day have not been studied.
Heart failure | 25 mg once a day for two weeks, or 12.5 mg once a day in more severe heart failure | Double the dose every two weeks to the highest dose you tolerate, up to 200 mg once a day.
Kapspargo Sprinkle capsules are not suitable to start heart failure treatment if a dose below 25 mg is needed.
Metoprolol dosage for children:
Extended-release metoprolol is the only form approved for children, and only for high blood pressure in children aged 6 years and older. The starting dose is 1 mg for each kilogram of body weight once a day, up to a maximum first dose of 50 mg. Doses above 2 mg/kg, or above 200 mg a day, have not been studied. Extended-release metoprolol has not been studied in children under 6 years.
Dose adjustments:
- Liver problems. Start at a lower dose than usual and increase slowly.
- Kidney problems. No dose reduction is needed.
- Older adults. A low starting dose is generally used, because liver, kidney, and heart function are more often reduced and other medicines are more often involved.
- Switching between forms. When changing from immediate-release to extended-release metoprolol, the same total daily dose is used.

Common Side Effects:
The most common tirzepatide side effects are:
- Diarrhea
- Vomiting
- Constipation
- Nausea (mild to moderate)
- Decreased appetite
- Abdominal pain.
Serious side effects:
Tirzepatide can cause serious side effects. Call your doctor right away if you have any of the following:

- Thyroid tumor: Symptoms may include a lump or swelling in your neck, trouble swallowing, hoarseness, or shortness of breath.

## How should I use levothyroxine?
Take levothyroxine exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Follow all directions on your prescription label and read all medication guides or instruction sheets. Your doctor may occasionally change your dose.
Some brands of levothyroxine have different dosage instructions and/or recommendations of how soon you need to take them before eating food. Always check the instructions on the label.
Oral levothyroxine:
Oral levothyroxine is taken by mouth and is available as tablets, capsules, and an oral solution.
- Keep using this medicine even if you feel well. It may take 4 to 6 weeks to get the full benefit of a dose.
- You will need frequent medical tests, and your next dose may be delayed based on the results.
- This medicine can affect the results of certain medical tests. Tell any doctor who treats you that you are using this medicine.
- Tell your doctor if you have a planned surgery or dental procedure.
- Taking more than your recommended dose will not make this medicine more effective, and may cause serious side effects.
Tablets and capsules:
Take levothyroxine tablets and capsules on an empty stomach, at least 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast with a full glass of water. A full glass of water is important to avoid choking or gagging, because the tablet can start to break apart quickly. Take the medicine at the same time each day.
- Swallow the capsule whole and do not crush, chew, break, or open it. Tell your doctor if your child cannot swallow a capsule whole.
- If you cannot swallow a tablet whole, crush the tablet and mix it with 1 or 2 teaspoons of water; give the mixture right away by spoon or dropper and make sure all of it is taken. Do not save it for later use. Do not mix it into soy-based infant formula or other foods that can stop levothyroxine being absorbed.
- Keep each tablet or capsule in the blister pack until you are ready to take one.
- Store at room temperature away from moisture, heat, and light.
Oral solution (liquid medicine):
Measure liquid medicine with the supplied measuring device (not a kitchen spoon).
- Dosages are based on weight in children and teenagers. Your child's dose may change if the child gains or loses weight.
- Your dose needs may change if you switch to a different brand, strength, or form of levothyroxine. Avoid medication errors by using only the medicine your doctor prescribes.
- Tirosint-Sol oral solution comes in single-dose ampules and can be administered 15 minutes before eating breakfast. Squeeze the liquid directly into your mouth, onto a spoon, or into a glass of water to drink right away. Use all ampules within 3 months after opening the foil pouch.
- Ermeza and Thyquidity liquids should be taken on an empty stomach, at least 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast. Store them in their original bottle. Use Ermeza within 90 days and Thyquidity within 8 weeks of opening the bottle.
- Store at room temperature away from moisture, heat, and light.
Intravenous levothyroxine:
This is given as an injection into a vein by a healthcare provider and should only be used to treat myxedema coma.
Blood tests, biotin, and monitoring:
Your doctor will use blood tests to check that your dose is right, usually 6 to 8 weeks after any dose change, and then every 6 to 12 months once your dose is stable. Children are tested more often, including 2 and 4 weeks after starting treatment and 2 weeks after any dose change.
Tell your doctor or pharmacist if you take biotin, or a multivitamin, hair, skin, or nail supplement that contains biotin (sometimes listed as vitamin B7). Biotin can interfere with thyroid blood tests and give a falsely high or falsely low result, which could lead to the wrong dose change. Stop biotin and any biotin-containing supplements at least 2 days before a thyroid blood test.
If your symptoms and blood tests still suggest an underactive thyroid even though you are on a dose that should be enough, it may be because the medicine is not being absorbed properly, doses are being missed, or another medicine is interfering. Talk to your doctor before your dose is increased.

## Dosing information
Usual Adult Dose for Hypertension:
Initial dose: 10 mg orally once a day; 5 mg orally once a day Maintenance dose: 20 to 40 mg orally once a day Maximum dose: 80 mg orally once a day Comments: -The initial dose is 5 mg orally once a day in patients receiving a diuretic. -The 80 mg dose is used but does not appear to give greater effect. -If blood pressure is not controlled with lisinopril alone, a low dose of a diuretic may be added (e.g., hydrochlorothiazide, 12.5 mg). After the addition of a diuretic, it may be possible to reduce the dose of lisinopril.
Usual Adult Dose for Congestive Heart Failure:
Initial dose: 2.5 to 5 mg orally once a day Maintenance dose: Dosage should be increased as tolerated Maximum dose: 40 mg orally once a day Comments: -The diuretic dose may need to be adjusted to help minimize hypovolemia, which may contribute to hypotension. The appearance of hypotension after the initial dose of lisinopril does not preclude subsequent careful dose titration with the drug.
Usual Adult Dose for Myocardial Infarction:
Initial dose: 5 mg orally (within 24 hours of the onset of acute myocardial infarction) Subsequent doses: 5 mg orally after 24 hours, then 10 mg orally after 48 hours. Maintenance dose: 10 mg orally once a day. Dosing should continue for at least 6 weeks. Comments: -Therapy should be initiated at 2.5 mg in patients with a low systolic blood pressure (less than or equal to 120 mm Hg and greater than 100 mmHg) during the first 3 days after the infarct. If prolonged hypotension occurs (systolic blood pressure less than 90 mmHg for more than 1 hour) therapy should be withdrawn. Uses: Reduction of mortality in acute myocardial infarction
Usual Adult Dose for Diabetic Nephropathy:
Initial dose: 10 to 20 mg orally once a day Maintenance dose: 20 to 40 mg orally once a day Dosage may be titrated upward every 3 days Comments: -Not an approved indication.
Usual Geriatric Dose for Hypertension:
Initial dose: 2.5 to 5 mg orally once a day Maintenance dose: Dosages should be increased at 2.5 mg to 5 mg per day at 1 to 2 week intervals. Maximum dose: 40 mg orally once a day
Usual Pediatric Dose for Hypertension:
Pediatric patients greater than or equal to 6 years of age: Initial dose: 0.07 mg/kg orally once a day (Maximum initial dose is 5 mg once a day) Maintenance dose: Dosage should be adjusted according to blood pressure response at 1 to 2 week intervals. Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to Adderall: hives, difficult breathing, or swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat.

Adderall may cause serious side effects. Call your doctor at once if you have:

Common side effects of Adderall may include stomach pain, loss of appetite, weight loss, mood changes, feeling nervous, fast heart rate, headache, dizziness, sleep problems (insomnia), and dry mouth.

## What other drugs will affect tamsulosin?
Tamsulosin is broken down in the body mainly by two liver enzymes, CYP3A4 and CYP2D6. Medicines that block these enzymes can raise the amount of tamsulosin in your blood and increase the risk of side effects.
Do not take tamsulosin with:
- strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as ketoconazole
- other alpha blockers, such as alfuzosin, doxazosin, prazosin, silodosin, or terazosin
Use with caution, and tell your doctor if you take:
- moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as erythromycin
- strong CYP2D6 inhibitors, such as paroxetine, or moderate CYP2D6 inhibitors, such as terbinafine
- cimetidine
- warfarin
- medicines for erectile dysfunction or pulmonary arterial hypertension known as PDE5 inhibitors, including avanafil (Stendra), sildenafil (Viagra, Revatio), tadalafil (Adcirca, Cialis), and vardenafil (Levitra). Taking these with tamsulosin can lower blood pressure enough to cause symptoms.
Some of these cautions matter more at the higher 0.8 mg dose than at 0.4 mg. Your doctor will decide what is right for you.
No dose change is needed if you take tamsulosin with nifedipine, atenolol, enalapril, digoxin, theophylline, or furosemide.
This list is not complete, and many other medicines may interact with tamsulosin. This includes prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal products.

Your doctor will use blood tests to check that your dose is right, usually 6 to 8 weeks after any dose change, and then every 6 to 12 months once your dose is stable. Children are tested more often, including 2 and 4 weeks after starting treatment and 2 weeks after any dose change.
Tell your doctor or pharmacist if you take biotin, or a multivitamin, hair, skin, or nail supplement that contains biotin (sometimes listed as vitamin B7). Biotin can interfere with thyroid blood tests and give a falsely high or falsely low result, which could lead to the wrong dose change. Stop biotin and any biotin-containing supplements at least 2 days before a thyroid blood test.
If your symptoms and blood tests still suggest an underactive thyroid even though you are on a dose that should be enough, it may be because the medicine is not being absorbed properly, doses are being missed, or another medicine is interfering. Talk to your doctor before your dose is increased.

## Hydrochlorothiazide side effects
The most noticeable effect of hydrochlorothiazide is passing urine more often, particularly in the first few weeks. This is how the medicine works rather than a side effect, and it usually settles as your body adjusts.
Serious side effects:
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction, such as hives, difficulty breathing, or swelling of your face, lips, tongue or throat.
Get emergency medical help if you have a severe skin reaction, such as a spreading red or purple rash with blistering and peeling, or skin that is painful to touch.
Stop taking hydrochlorothiazide and get medical help immediately if you have a sudden change in your vision or pain in your eye.
Call your doctor at once if you have:
- severe pain in your upper stomach that spreads to your back, with nausea and vomiting, which can be a sign of inflammation of the pancreas (pancreatitis)
- yellowing of your skin or the whites of your eyes (jaundice)
- fever, chills, sore throat, mouth sores or other signs of infection
- unusual bruising or bleeding, or pale skin and unusual tiredness, which can be signs of a blood problem
- shortness of breath, wheezing, or a cough with frothy mucus
- passing much less urine than usual, or swelling in your legs and ankles
- light-headedness or fainting, especially when standing up
- signs of dehydration or a salt imbalance, such as extreme thirst, dry mouth, confusion, muscle cramps, irregular heartbeat or unusual weakness
Other side effects:
Other hydrochlorothiazide side effects include:
- dizziness, a spinning sensation (vertigo), headache, restlessness, or tingling and numbness (paresthesia)
- weakness
- nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, stomach cramping, stomach irritation, or loss of appetite
- muscle spasm
- increased sensitivity to sunlight, causing sunburn more easily
- hair loss or thinning
- difficulty getting or keeping an erection
- temporary blurred vision, or objects looking yellow-tinged (xanthopsia)
- swelling and tenderness of the salivary glands
- raised blood sugar, sugar in the urine, or raised uric acid
If a side effect is moderate or severe, your doctor may lower your dose or stop the medicine. Do not stop taking HCTZ on your own without speaking to your doctor first.
This is not a complete list of side effects and others may occur. Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects. You may report side effects to the FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.

## Warnings
Meloxicam can increase your risk of a fatal heart attack or stroke, especially if you use it long term or take high doses, or if you have heart disease. Even people without heart disease or risk factors could have a stroke or heart attack while taking this medicine.
Do not use this medicine just before or after heart bypass surgery (coronary artery bypass graft, or CABG).
Avoid taking meloxicam after a recent heart attack, unless your doctor tells you to. You may have an increased risk of another heart attack if you take this medicine after a recent heart attack.
Get emergency medical help if you have chest pain, weakness, shortness of breath, slurred speech, or problems with vision or balance.
Meloxicam may also cause stomach or intestinal bleeding, which can be fatal. These conditions can occur without warning while you are using this medicine, especially in older adults.
Call your doctor at once if you have symptoms of stomach bleeding, such as black, bloody, or tarry stools, or coughing up blood or vomit that looks like coffee grounds.
Avoid smoking and drinking alcohol, as they also increase your risk of stomach bleeding.

## What is montelukast?
Montelukast helps to reduce inflammation and may be used to prevent asthma attacks in adults and children at least 2 years old.
Montelukast is also used to prevent exercise-induced bronchoconstriction (a narrowing of the air passages in the lungs due to exercise that is also known as exercise-induced asthma) in adults and children who are at least 6 years old.
For adults and children at least 2 years old with symptoms of seasonal allergic rhinitis, and people over 6 months old with perennial (year-round) allergies, montelukast may be considered when other treatments have not worked.
If you already take montelukast regularly to prevent asthma or allergy symptoms, do not take an extra dose to treat exercise-induced bronchoconstriction.
Montelukast is not a fast-acting rescue medicine for asthma attacks and needs to be taken daily to work properly.
Montelukast was FDA-approved in 1998.

## Prednisone FAQs
Is prednisone a steroid?:
Yes. Prednisone is a corticosteroid, also called a glucocorticoid. Corticosteroids are copies of hormones your adrenal glands make naturally, and they work by lowering inflammation and immune activity. They are not the same as the anabolic steroids some athletes misuse to build muscle.
How long does it take for prednisone to work?:
Prednisone starts to be absorbed within about an hour, and many people notice a difference in symptoms such as swelling, pain, or wheezing within a few hours to a day. Some conditions take several days or longer to respond. Delayed-release tablets are designed to release the medicine about four hours after you take them, so the timing of your dose matters.
How long does prednisone stay in your system?:
Prednisone and prednisolone have a half-life of about 2 to 3 hours, which means half of a dose leaves your blood in that time. Most of a single dose is out of your bloodstream within about a day.
The effect lasts longer than the drug itself. A single dose of prednisone quiets your own adrenal glands for about one and a quarter to one and a half days, which is why prednisone is described as short-acting compared with steroids such as dexamethasone. This is also why a course of prednisone can affect your blood sugar, your sleep, and your energy for longer than the drug is measurable in your blood.
Why has my doctor prescribed prednisone every other day?:
Alternate day dosing means taking twice your usual daily dose every other morning instead of a dose every day. It is used for people who need steroid treatment for a long time. Giving your body a day off from the steroid lets your adrenal glands recover between doses, which reduces the risk of adrenal suppression, Cushing's syndrome, withdrawal symptoms, and slowed growth in children.
The trade-off is that your symptoms may flare a little late in the day you do not take it. Tell your doctor if this happens, since other treatment can often be added for that gap. Do not switch yourself to an every other day schedule, and do not double up on a day you were not meant to take a dose.
What is the difference between prednisone and prednisolone?:
Prednisone has to be converted by your liver into prednisolone before it can work, while prednisolone is already in the active form. For most people the two work in a very similar way at equivalent doses. Prednisolone is often chosen for people with significant liver disease, and for children, because it comes in liquid forms that are easier to dose.
Does prednisone cause weight gain?:
Weight gain is a common side effect of prednisone. It happens for two reasons. Prednisone makes your body hold onto salt and water, which adds weight quickly in the first days or weeks, and it increases appetite, which adds body fat over longer courses. It also moves fat toward the face, neck, upper back and waist. Weight from fluid usually goes once you stop, but weight from extra eating takes longer to shift.
Can you drink alcohol while taking prednisone?:
There is no direct interaction between alcohol and prednisone, but drinking is best kept to a minimum. Both irritate the stomach lining, so together they raise the risk of stomach ulcers and bleeding. Alcohol also raises blood sugar and weakens bones, and prednisone does both of these too. Ask your doctor what is reasonable for you, especially if you are on a long course.
Can you take ibuprofen with prednisone?:
It is usually best to avoid ibuprofen while you are taking prednisone. Ibuprofen is an NSAID, and taking an NSAID with a steroid raises the risk of stomach ulcers and bleeding. The same applies to naproxen, diclofenac, and regular doses of aspirin. If you need a painkiller, ask your doctor or pharmacist first.
Can you take Tylenol with prednisone?:
Acetaminophen (Tylenol) does not interact with prednisone and does not irritate the stomach, so it is generally the preferred choice for pain or fever while you are taking prednisone. Stay within the recommended daily limit on the packet and check whether any other product you take already contains acetaminophen.
Why does prednisone keep me awake?:
Prednisone acts like your body's stress hormone, which naturally peaks in the morning to help you wake up. Taking it, especially later in the day, can leave you feeling wired, restless or unable to sleep. Taking your dose in the morning often helps. Talk to your doctor before changing when you take it.
Does prednisone raise blood pressure?:
It can. Prednisone makes your body hold onto salt and water, which raises blood pressure in some people, particularly at higher doses or on longer courses. Your blood pressure should be checked during treatment, and your doctor may ask you to reduce salt in your diet.
What is considered a high dose of prednisone?:
There is no official cutoff, but doctors generally treat doses under 7.5 mg a day as low, 7.5 mg to 40 mg a day as moderate, and more than 40 mg a day as high. A dose of 20 mg a day sits in the moderate range. What matters as much as the number is how long you take it, because side effects build up over time.
Can prednisone make you tired?:
Yes. Some people feel energized on prednisone while others feel drained. Poor sleep, mood changes and muscle weakness all contribute. Tiredness that starts as your dose is being lowered, or after you stop, can be a sign that your adrenal glands have not caught up yet, so tell your doctor if it is severe or comes with dizziness, nausea, or body aches.

## What is losartan?
Losartan is used alone or in combination with other medications to treat high blood pressure in adults and children at least 6 years old.
Losartan is also used to decrease the risk of stroke in people who have high blood pressure and a heart condition called left ventricular hypertrophy (enlargement of the walls of the left side of the heart).
Losartan may not decrease the risk of stroke in African Americans who have these conditions.
Losartan is also used to treat kidney disease in people who have type 2 diabetes (condition in which the body does not use insulin normally and therefore cannot control the amount of sugar in the blood) and high blood pressure.
Losartan belongs to a class of medications called angiotensin II receptor antagonists. It works by blocking the action of certain natural substances that tighten the blood vessels, allowing the blood to flow more smoothly and the heart to pump more efficiently.

## Metoprolol dosage
The usual starting dose is 25 mg to 100 mg once a day for extended-release metoprolol, and 100 mg a day for immediate-release metoprolol. Your dose is then adjusted at intervals of a week or longer until your blood pressure or symptoms are controlled.
Metoprolol tartrate (immediate-release tablets) dosage for adults:
Condition | Starting dose | Usual range
High blood pressure | 100 mg a day, as one dose or split into two | 100 mg to 450 mg a day. Doses above 450 mg a day have not been studied.
Angina | 100 mg a day, split into two doses | 100 mg to 400 mg a day. Doses above 400 mg a day have not been studied.
After a heart attack | 50 mg every 6 hours for 48 hours, starting 15 minutes after the last dose given into a vein. If the full intravenous dose was not tolerated, 25 mg is used. | Maintenance is 100 mg twice a day, continued for at least 3 months.
With immediate-release tablets, a once-daily dose may not keep blood pressure controlled for the full 24 hours, especially at 100 mg. Splitting the dose or taking a larger daily dose may be needed.
Metoprolol succinate (extended-release tablets and capsules) dosage for adults:
Condition | Starting dose | Usual range
High blood pressure | 25 mg to 100 mg once a day | Adjust weekly or less often. Doses above 400 mg a day have not been studied.
Angina | 100 mg once a day | Increase weekly until symptoms are controlled or your heart rate slows noticeably. Doses above 400 mg a day have not been studied.
Heart failure | 25 mg once a day for two weeks, or 12.5 mg once a day in more severe heart failure | Double the dose every two weeks to the highest dose you tolerate, up to 200 mg once a day.
Kapspargo Sprinkle capsules are not suitable to start heart failure treatment if a dose below 25 mg is needed.
Metoprolol dosage for children:
Extended-release metoprolol is the only form approved for children, and only for high blood pressure in children aged 6 years and older. The starting dose is 1 mg for each kilogram of body weight once a day, up to a maximum first dose of 50 mg. Doses above 2 mg/kg, or above 200 mg a day, have not been studied. Extended-release metoprolol has not been studied in children under 6 years.
Dose adjustments:
- Liver problems. Start at a lower dose than usual and increase slowly.
- Kidney problems. No dose reduction is needed.
- Older adults. A low starting dose is generally used, because liver, kidney, and heart function are more often reduced and other medicines are more often involved.
- Switching between forms. When changing from immediate-release to extended-release metoprolol, the same total daily dose is used.

## How should I use Flonase Nasal Spray?
Use Flonase exactly as directed on the label, or as prescribed by your doctor. Follow all directions on your prescription label and read all medication guides or instruction sheets.
Do not share this medicine with another person, even if they have the same symptoms you have. Sharing a bottle can spread germs.
Your dose will depend on the fluticasone brand or strength you use, and your dose may change once your symptoms improve. Follow all dosing instructions very carefully.
- A child using the nasal spray should be supervised by an adult.
Read and carefully follow any Instructions for Use provided with your medicine. Ask your doctor or pharmacist if you do not understand these instructions.
Shake the bottle before each use. Flonase Allergy Relief should be shaken gently, and Flonase Sensimist should be shaken vigorously.
Use this product only once a day and do not use more than directed. Avoid getting the spray in your eyes or mouth.
If you switched to fluticasone from another steroid medicine, you should not stop using it suddenly. Follow your doctor's instructions about tapering your dose.
Storage differs between products. Store Flonase Allergy Relief and Children's Flonase Allergy Relief between 4°C and 30°C (39°F and 86°F). Store Flonase Sensimist between 15°C and 30°C (59°F and 86°F), and do not refrigerate or freeze it.
Throw the bottle away once you have used the number of sprays stated on the carton, even if there is still liquid in the bottle. The correct amount of medicine in each spray cannot be assured after the labeled number of sprays has been used. Bottle sizes vary between products and pack sizes, ranging from 30 to 144 metered sprays.
Dosing information:
Usual Adult Dose for Rhinitis (adults and children 12 years of age and older):
Flonase Allergy Relief Nasal Spray (fluticasone propionate 50 mcg per spray):
- Week 1: use 2 sprays in each nostril once daily
- Week 2 through 6 months: use 1 or 2 sprays in each nostril once daily, as needed to treat your symptoms
- After 6 months of daily use: ask your doctor if you can keep using this medicine
Flonase Sensimist Nasal Spray (fluticasone furoate 27.5 mcg per spray):
- Week 1: use 2 sprays in each nostril once daily
- Week 2 through 6 months: use 1 or 2 sprays in each nostril once daily, as needed to treat your symptoms
- After 6 months of daily use: ask your doctor if you can keep using this medicine
Usual Pediatric Dose for Rhinitis:
- 4 to 11 years: Flonase Allergy Relief or Children's Flonase Allergy Relief (fluticasone propionate 50 mcg per spray): 1 spray in each nostril once daily.
- 2 to 11 years: Flonase Sensimist or Children's Flonase Sensimist (fluticasone furoate 27.5 mcg per spray): 1 spray in each nostril once daily.
- Under 4 years: do not use fluticasone propionate nasal spray.
- Under 2 years: do not use fluticasone furoate nasal spray.
An adult should supervise a child using the spray. Children should use it for the shortest amount of time necessary to achieve symptom relief. Talk to your child's doctor if your child needs to use the spray for longer than two months a year.
What happens if I miss a dose?:
Use the medicine as soon as you can, but skip the missed dose if it is almost time for your next dose. Do not use two doses at one time.
What happens if I overdose?:
Seek emergency medical attention or call the Poison Help line at 1-800-222-1222.
An overdose of Flonase is not expected to produce life-threatening symptoms. Using more than the recommended dose, or using it for longer than directed, may increase the chance of corticosteroid-related side effects such as cataracts or glaucoma, adrenal gland problems, an increased risk of infection, sores inside the nose, or slower growth in children.

## How should I take carvedilol?
Take carvedilol exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Follow all directions on your prescription label. Your doctor may occasionally change your dose to make sure you get the best results. Do not take this medicine in larger or smaller amounts or for longer than recommended.
Take carvedilol with food.
Swallow the extended-release capsule whole and do not crush or chew it. If you have trouble swallowing, you may open the carvedilol capsule and sprinkle the medicine into a spoonful of applesauce to make swallowing easier. The applesauce should not be warm. Do not sprinkle contents on foods other than applesauce. Swallow right away without chewing. Do not save the mixture for later use. Discard the empty capsule.
Take carvedilol at the same time every day. Do not skip doses or stop taking carvedilol without first talking to your doctor. Stopping suddenly may cause chest pain or a heart attack.
If you are switched from carvedilol tablets to carvedilol extended-release capsules (Coreg CR), your daily total dose of this medicine may be higher or lower than before. Older adults may be more likely to become dizzy or feel faint when switching from tablets to extended-release capsules. Follow your doctor's instructions.
Your blood pressure will need to be checked often.
If you are being treated for high blood pressure, keep using this medication even if you feel well. High blood pressure often has no symptoms. You may need to use blood pressure medication for the rest of your life.
If you need surgery, tell the surgeon ahead of time that you are using carvedilol. You may need to stop using the medicine for a short time.
You should not stop using carvedilol suddenly. Stopping suddenly may cause chest pain or a heart attack.
Carvedilol can affect your pupils during cataract surgery. Tell your eye surgeon ahead of time that you are using this medication. Do not stop using carvedilol before surgery unless your surgeon tells you to.
Carvedilol is only part of a complete program of treatment for hypertension that may also include diet, exercise, and weight control. Follow your diet, medication, and exercise routines very closely if you are being treated for hypertension.
Store at room temperature away from moisture and heat.

## How should I use albuterol inhalation?
Use albuterol inhalation exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Follow all directions on your prescription label. Do not use albuterol inhalation in larger or smaller amounts or for longer than recommended.
Read all patient information, medication guides, and instruction sheets provided to you. Ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions.
You may need to prime your albuterol inhaler device before the first use. Your medicine comes with directions for priming if needed. You may also need to shake your albuterol device just before each use.
Keeping your inhaler clean is important to ensure you are receiving the medication. Clean the plastic actuator with the canister removed at least once a week. Your medicine comes with directions for properly cleaning your device.
Follow all medication instructions very carefully.
Do not allow a young child to use albuterol inhalation without help from an adult.
The usual dose of albuterol inhalation is 2 inhalations every 4 to 6 hours. To prevent exercise-induced bronchospasm, use 2 inhalations 15 to 30 minutes before you exercise. The effects of albuterol inhalation should last about 4 to 6 hours.
Seek medical attention if you think your asthma medications are not working as well. An increased need for medication could be an early sign of a serious asthma attack.
Use the dose counter on your albuterol inhaler device and get your prescription refilled before you run out of medicine completely. Always use the new inhaler device provided with your refill. Do not float a medicine canister in water to see if it is empty.
ProAir HFA, Proventil HFA, or Ventolin HFA must be shaken before each use. You do not need to shake ProAir RespiClick before using.
Follow all product instructions on how to clean your albuterol inhaler device and mouthpiece. Do not wash or put any part of the ProAir RespiClick inhaler device in water. Replace your inhaler if it is washed or placed in water. If the mouthpiece needs cleaning, gently wipe it with a dry cloth or tissue. Do not use a spacer or volume holding chamber with ProAir RespiClick.
Asthma is often treated with a combination of drugs. Use all medications as directed by your doctor. Read the medication guide or patient instructions provided with each medication. Do not change your doses or medication schedule without your doctor's advice.
Store at room temperature away from moisture, heat, or cold temperatures.
Keep the albuterol canister away from open flame or high heat, such as in a car on a hot day. The canister may explode if it gets too hot. Do not puncture or burn an empty inhaler canister.

Common sertraline side effects:
The most common sertraline side effects are nausea, diarrhea or loose stools, trouble sleeping, dry mouth, tiredness, dizziness, sleepiness, tremor, indigestion, agitation, reduced appetite, increased sweating, and sexual problems.
The table below shows how often each side effect was reported in pooled placebo-controlled trials in 3,066 adults, compared with 2,293 people taking placebo.
